/* PRINT SIZES, THE FRACTION CASE. `.fr` is `.86em` of whatever it sits
   in — fine for maths, which sets its own `.dm` big enough (19px/17.5px
   acol) to absorb that step down and still clear the floor. Physical
   chemistry's molality/mole-fraction formulas are the first chemistry
   content to lean on stacked fractions this heavily, and chemistry's `.dm`
   is smaller (18px/16.5px acol) for reaction-line reasons unrelated to
   fractions at all — `.86em` of the acol figure is 14.2px, 10.4px printed,
   under the 11px floor. Same fix as `.rxn-t`/`.sp-u` above: an absolute
   floor px instead of a fraction of the container. */
.subj-chemistry .fr { font-size:15px; }
.subj-chemistry .acol .fr { font-size:15px; }

/* UPRIGHT, NOT ITALIC — the one typographic rule chemistry has.
   An element symbol is roman: SOCl₂, not SOCl₂ in italic. Italic is
   reserved for a physical quantity (p, V, T), which is why physics
   sets its whole maths run that way. Chemistry inherited that face
   and every formula on the page came out slanted, which is what made
   the reactions read as sloppy beside a reference textbook — the
   glyphs were right and the posture was wrong. */
.subj-chemistry .m, .subj-chemistry .dm, .subj-chemistry .work
  { font-style:normal; }
.subj-chemistry .rxn>.rxn-t, .subj-chemistry .rxn>.rxn-b,
.subj-chemistry .sp>.sp-u, .subj-chemistry .sp>.sp-o
  { font-style:normal; }

/* THE GUTTER IS THE PADDING, NOT A SEPARATE GAP.
   `acols/a4.rules.json` already widened `.acol:first-child`/
   `:last-child` padding to 32px a side (64px total) so a matrix
   or a grid structure clears the dashed divider. Adding a 72px
   `column-gap` here on top of that, meant to give the same rule
   more room, instead stacked two fixes for one problem: 64px of
   padding plus 72px of gap put 136px of dead space either side
   of the line, which read as far too much empty margin between
   the columns and the text. Removed — the padding alone was
   already the deliberate fix.
   Do not recolour or restyle the divider rule itself here — a
   past attempt to soften it to grey via `.acols::before` was a
   dead selector (`::before` never got a `content`), and a second
   attempt via `.acol+.acol` border-left just drew a SECOND line
   beside the first instead of replacing it. Both removed; the
   base `.acols::after` blue dashed rule is the only one. */

/* THE EQUATION AS A UNIT — reactants | arrow | products.
   A flex row, so every species in the equation shares a baseline and the
   arrow cannot drift from either side of it. `nowrap` on a SIDE is still
   the rule: a chemical structure's geometry is chemistry, not
   typesetting, and `CH₃—CH—CH₂—Br` with a bond hanging under the middle
   carbon must never be broken mid-formula.

   THE ROW ITSELF WRAPS. A reaction with a drawn ring on each side, or
   two molecules on one side joined by `+` (a Wurtz-Fittig reactant: a
   ring plus a small molecule), is often wider than a narrow column no
   matter how small the rings are drawn. Held to one line, that width
   had nowhere to go but sideways into whatever sat next to it — see the
   `.rxn-side` note below. Wrapped, the side that does not fit drops to
   its own line under the rest of the equation instead: still one
   equation, just two rows, which is worse than one row but far better
   than a ring painted on top of the arrow's own label.

   `.rxn-side` MUST ALSO REFUSE TO SHRINK. `.rxn` was given `flex:none`
   but `.rxn-side` was not, so it kept the flex default of `flex-shrink:1`
   — a side with two drawn rings in it was squeezed narrower than its own
   children's combined width whenever the equation as a whole did not fit
   its column. The rings inside do not shrink with it (they are not flex
   items of `.rxn-eq` themselves), so they painted at full size and
   spilled out of the shrunken box — straight into the arrow's reagent
   label sitting next to it. That is what read as a giant, misplaced `Cl`
   glyph overlapping the arrow. Protecting the side the same way the
   arrow is protected, TOGETHER with the wrap above, means an oversized
   equation grows a second row instead of overlapping the first. */
.rxn-eq { display:inline-flex; flex-wrap:wrap; align-items:center;
     justify-content:flex-start; gap:2px 4px; row-gap:6px; max-width:100%; }
.rxn-eq>.rxn-side { white-space:nowrap; flex-shrink:0; }
.rxn-eq>.rxn { flex:none; }
/* A SIDE WITH TWO DRAWN RINGS ON IT MUST ALSO BE ALLOWED TO WRAP.
   `.rxn-side { white-space:nowrap }` above exists to keep ONE typed
   formula (`CH₃—CH—CH₂—Br`) from breaking mid-structure — necessary,
   because that side is text. A Fittig or Wurtz-Fittig reactant
   (`chlorobenzene + chlorobenzene`, joined by `+`) is a DIFFERENT
   shape: two whole, separately-drawn rings that happen to sit in the
   same `.rxn-side`. `nowrap` does not know that distinction — it held
   both rings on one unbreakable line even when their combined width
   ran past the edge of the page, which is what printed a ring cut off
   mid-structure with its label truncated to a single letter. A side
   that CONTAINS a drawn ring can safely wrap at the `+` between
   molecules — that boundary was never inside one structure's bonds —
   so it gets its own flex row instead of the plain nowrap text rule. */
.rxn-side:has(.cring) { white-space:normal; display:inline-flex;
     flex-wrap:wrap; align-items:center; gap:2px 6px; }
/* A species stack is one object too — the name below and the charge
   above travel with the formula they belong to. */
.sp { white-space:nowrap; }

/* THE GLYPH MUST SIT UNDER ITS OWN LABEL.
   `.rxn` is a three-row grid — label, arrow, label — at least 44px
   wide, and `.rxn>.rxn-a` is `width:100%` because a plain arrow DRAWS
   itself with a border across that whole width. A harpoon does not:
   it drops the border and puts a `\u21cc` character in `::after`, which
   then sits at the LEFT edge of the 44px row while the label above it
   is centred over the row. That is the gap between `\u092e\u0928\u094d\u0926` and the
   equilibrium arrow in the S\u0274 1 first step. Same for the both-ways
   arrow, which is built the same way. */
.rxn-harpoon>.rxn-a, .rxn-both>.rxn-a { text-align:center; }
